items.title: Beyond ‘cleaning’ voter rolls: The digital machinery behind SIR
items.summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Indian government have consistently framed the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) as a routine and much-needed clean-up of India’s electoral rolls. In reality, however, it marks a deep shift. The push to use software systems to sanitise electoral rolls could be traced to the early 2000s with the explosion of the Information Technology industry. Despite the massive relevance of these systems in our democracy, the ECI has publicly disclosed very little about their algorithms and software architecture. The goal is no longer maintaining unique voters in the electoral system with no duplicate records. With the SIR, the goal is also to create a tech-driven, centralised, algorithmic mapping of individuals, their networks, familial and marital ties. The technology behind SIR could pave the way for increasing centralisation and automation of electoral roll management. This raises questions about who ultimately makes decisions about inclusion and exclusion from the electoral roll, what role election officials retain, and whether the technology being used is subject to the transparency and safeguards that govern the electoral process.
